question.prompt: How many of the first ten numbers of the sequence \[121, 11211, 1112111, \ldots\] are prime numbers?

solutions.title: Overlap two strings of ones
solutions.explanation:
The middle digit \(2\) can come from adding two strings of ones that overlap in exactly one position. This gives a factorization; for example,
\[
11211=11100+111=111(100+1).
\]
For the \(n\)th term, there are \(n\) ones on each side of the \(2\). Let \(R\) be the integer consisting of \(n+1\) ones. Multiplying \(R\) by \(10^n\) shifts its digits \(n\) places to the left. When we add \(R\) back, the two strings overlap only at the middle position. That position becomes \(2\), all other digits are \(1\), and no carrying occurs.

Thus the \(n\)th term equals
\[
10^nR+R=(10^n+1)R.
\]
For every \(n\geq1\), both factors are at least \(11\), so every term is composite. In particular, the first ten terms contain \(\boxed{0}\) prime numbers, choice \(\textbf{A}\).
